character_sheet: A large passive dragonfly: a thorax with a head, two jaws, antennae, six jointed legs, a two-part tail and four long wings. It hunts small prey on the wing and is otherwise calm. Read it as a fast four-winged flyer with a slowly working mouth.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.5 of the rig on a 64x64 sheet.

groups.name: wings
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg); the rear pair carries a +3.14 rad (half-turn) offset
groups.plain: the four wings beat fast about the body's long axis: front-left up while front-right is down, the rear pair the same shape turned half round
groups.math: lfwing.zRot = cos(ageInTicks * 1.3 * 2.0) * pi * 0.25; rfwing.zRot = -(that); lrwing.zRot = that + 3.14; rrwing.zRot = -(that) + 3.14
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x 2 (two float multiplies, left to right): the natural period is 2 pi / 2.6

groups.name: jaws
groups.plain: the two jaws open and close slowly, mirrored (they bind tilted 0.436 rad about X, the keys carry the delta)
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.3 x 2 (two float multiplies, left to right): the natural period is 2 pi / 0.6

behaviour: Several independent rhythms run at all times, none scaled by walking speed; the classic code has no rest pose. The transcription ships idle (no bone) plus one clip per rhythm: the primary group (`primary_group`; the first group when the seed names none) carries the bare `walk` - a label, not a semantic: the contract's fly -> walk fallback is what plays a flyer's walk in flight (owner 2026-09-13, addendum item 26 (2)) - and every other rhythm is `walk_<group>`, so the GeckoLib candidate plays the transcription behind the switch.
Two rhythms: the fast wing beat (the primary group: its clip is the bare walk) and the slow jaws; legs, tail, head and antennae are static.

The default renderer poses it from the classic code; the GeckoLib candidate sits behind the dev switch (-Dorespawn.dev.geckolibRenderers) and your clips replace the shipped transcription file for file.
